chunks: And whatever is in it from Ayyub ibn al-Harr, I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan—may Allah be pleased with him—from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Ayyub ibn al-Harr al-Ju'fi al-Kufi, the brother of Adim ibn al-Harr, and he was a freed slave.

key_terms.أَيُّوبَ بْنِ الْحُرِّ: A transmitter whose chain is being clarified here
key_terms.الصَّفَّارِ: A major narrator in the transmission chain
key_terms.الْبَرْقِيِّ: A known transmitter in the sanad
key_terms.الْجُعْفِيِّ الْكُوفِيِّ: A tribal and regional attribution identifying Ayyub ibn al-Harr
key_terms.مَوْلًى: A freed slave or client affiliate

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to Ayyub ibn al-Harr in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage is a sanad clarification identifying the transmission route for narrations attributed to Ayyub ibn al-Harr in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih. It preserves both the chain of narrators and a brief biographical note about Ayyub ibn al-Harr al-Ju'fi al-Kufi.
